newsitem.title: GHANA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
GHANA, Sept 9-23 - Tema, Takoradi - No waiting time.

ISRAEL, Sept 10 - Haifa - Ten vessels berthed operating of which 7 discharging (5 general cargo, 2 bulkers), 3 container vessels. 6 Waiting at anchorage of which 5 to discharge (2 general cargo, 3 bulkers), 1 container. 1 bunkering, 5 under repair/dry-docked, 2 awaiting orders. 5 due, 1-2 days delay. Ashdod - Ten vessels berthed operating of which 7 discharging (5 general cargo, 2 bulkers), 3 containers, 5 waiting at anchorage of which 2 to discharge general cargo, 3 to load bulk cargo. 1 Bunkering, 1 under repair/dry-docked. 1-2 days delay. Eilat - Two berthed and operating of which 1 bulker loading, 1 car carrier discharging, 1 bulker waiting to load, 2 due.
JORDAN, Sept 7 - Aqaba three vessels loading at berth, 3 discharging, 8 waiting to load, 3 to discharge, 3 awaiting orders.

MAURITIUS, Sept 10 - Port Louis - No strikes. Two vessels berthed discharging/loading containers, 3 discharging general cargo, 1 berthed at buoys discharging rice into lighters. No idle vessels, 1 dry-docked, 2 at outer anchorage awaiting berths for discharging containers and general cargo respectively. Fishing port very busy, bunching of Taiwanese and Japanese vessels calling for transhipment/discharging of fish and bunkering.

MOZAMBIQUE, Sept 9 - Nacala - Port working normally on first come, first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restriction 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths, 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally, first come, first served basis. Container/other terminals working normally. Pilotage in daylight only. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation by special arrangement, restricted to 130 metres LOA. Maputo - Pilotage in daylight only. Two tugs, one out of order. All berths working normally, expected to remain so (first come, first served). Draft restriction in channel nine metres less 0.5 metre plus rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Sept 9 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SIERRA LEONE, Sept 9 - Freetown - Three rice dischargers berthed and operating, 1 general cargo vessel anchored under arrest, 4 vessels due (2 container dischargers, 1 container/vehicles discharger, 1 bulk wheat discharger). No delays expected. Vessels must endeavour to be in/out of port before 1900 hrs. Weather rainy with intermittent sunshine.

SOUTH AFRICA, Sept 9 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths fully committed. Bulk import berths fully committed, delays of up to 15 days. Bulk export working normally, but could change. Berth 701 out of commission from 5-12/9 due to dredging. Bulk coal 3 vessels berthed, 3 anchored, 18 due in the next week, up to and including 16/9. Berthing delays up to 3 days. Durban container terminal delays to 96 hours. Point, New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Working normally. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - 6 Maize loaders for September. Citrus terminal - Tapering off as season closes towards end-September. Bunker supplies tight. Delays in supplying bunkers due to bunching of vessels.

Dry/floating dock fully booked for September, 70 percent booked for october. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths extremely busy but no delays. Dry-dock fully booked for September and first two weeks of October then open. Copper moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month to Far East. Elevator extremely busy with 4-5 days delay. Gas oil pipeline under-utilised. Log loaders 15,000 cbm on hand awaiting shipment. Scrap steel 5,500 tonnes on hand awaiting shipment. Tankers 1 vessel due 10/9. Port Elizabeth - Working normally, 6 vessels in port. No delays on general, fruit, ore, tanker, or container berths. Three gantry cranes available at all times. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths no delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal - No delays expected for coming week. Two new gantry cranes now fully operational. Bunker berths - No days foreseen for coming week. Dry-dock and repair quay fully occupied, advance booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, Sept 7 - Sfax - Three vessels operating of which 2 loading (1 bulk tsp, 1 rock phosphate), 1 under repair. Sousse - No vessels in port, none due by weekend. Gabes - One loading at berth, 3 discharging (1 bulk sulphur, 1 liquid sulphur, 1 fluorspar), no vessels waiting at anchor. Sept 10 - Bizerte - No delays/congestion/strikes. Five vessels operating, 3 loading (1 cement, 1 bran, 1 fuel oil), 2 discharging (steel, timber). Zarzis - No delays/congestion/strikes/vessels.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - Dubai - Port operations 1-7 september - One hundred and seventy-nine vessels of which 70 containers, 15 general cargo, 5 general cargo/containers, 6 bulk carriers, 2 car carriers, , 1 livestock carrier, 19 tankers, 1 UAE naval vessel. 4 Bunkering/under repair/taking stores etc., 5 dhows, 9 barges, 10 tugs, 5 lpg tankers, 26 supply boats, 1 landing craft. No waiting time. Dubai, Sept 7 - Nine vessels loading at berth of which 6 containers, 3 tankers. 4 General cargo vessels discharging at berth. 1 Container vessel bunkering. 15 Vessels under repair/laid up of which 2 containers, 5 general cargo, 8 tankers. 38 Vessels due of which 28 containers, 6 general cargo and 4 tankers, all with no delays expected.

YEMEN, Sept 8 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied, 7 vessels berthed of which 3 sugar, 2 wheat flour, 1 general cargo, 1 loading general cargo, 1 container vessel waiting at anchor. Berthing delays general cargo up to 2 days, bagged up to 4 days, Bulk up to 6 days. Containers up to 1 day. Mokha - No vessels berthed, none anchored, no berthing delays.
